title: Finite filtered objects have enough injectives for strict monomorphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Use finite decreasing filtrations and filtration-preserving maps [def-sp-filtration]. Call a monomorphism $u:X\to Y$ strict if $u(F^pX)=u(X)\cap F^pY$ for every integer $p$, and call a filtered object $I$ filtered injective if every $\operatorname{gr}^pI$ is injective in the extension-property sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every strict monomorphism $u:X\to Y$, every filtered injective $I$, and every filtration-preserving $f:X\to I$, there exists a filtration-preserving $g:Y\to I$ with $gu=f$. If $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives (every object embeds into an injective object), every finite filtered object $X$ admits a strict monomorphism $X\to I$ with $I$ filtered injective. Moreover, if $F^aX=X$ and $F^{b+1}X=0$ for fixed integers $a\le b$, $I$ can be chosen with these same bounds.

source.place: Tags 05TR (lemma-injective-property-filtered-injective) and 05TS (lemma-strict-monomorphism-into-filtered-injective); same-interval choice is the displayed finite direct-sum construction in the proof of 05TS

proof.text: Choose bounds $c\le d$ for the finite filtration on the target $I$. Apply [lem-trf-injective-graded-filtration-splits] to obtain a filtered isomorphism $\theta:I\cong\bigoplus_{n=c}^d J_n$, with $J_n$ injective and $F^pI$ identified with the summands indexed by $n\ge p$. Write $f_n:X\to J_n$ for the components of $\theta f$. The summand projection to $J_n$ vanishes on $F^{n+1}I$, so $f_n$ vanishes on $F^{n+1}X$.

For $c\le n\le d$ let $\bar u_n:X/F^{n+1}X\to Y/F^{n+1}Y$ be induced by $u$. Its kernel is zero: the inverse image of $F^{n+1}Y$ under $u$ is $F^{n+1}X$, precisely the strictness equality after identifying $X$ with $u(X)$. Equivalently, the kernel of $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\to Y/F^{n+1}Y$ is $F^{n+1}X$, so passage to its quotient gives a monomorphism $\bar u_n$. This is the kernel/quotient universal-property calculation in the abelian category [def-sp-abelian], using the subobject and quotient conventions of [def-sp-filtration]. The vanishing from Step 1 factors $f_n$ through a map $\bar f_n:X/F^{n+1}X\to J_n$.

source.place: Tag 05TR, lemma-injective-property-filtered-injective; elementary quotient form of strictness

proof.text: By the defining extension property [def-sp-injective-resolutions], extend $\bar f_n$ across the monomorphism $\bar u_n$ to $h_n:Y/F^{n+1}Y\to J_n$. Set $g_n=h_nq_n$, where $q_n:Y\to Y/F^{n+1}Y$, and use the finite biproduct [def-sp-abelian] to assemble $g=\theta^{-1}(g_c,\ldots,g_d):Y\to I$. Each component satisfies $g_nu=f_n$, hence $gu=f$. For any $p$, every component with $n<p$ vanishes on $F^pY$, because $F^pY\subseteq F^{n+1}Y$ [def-sp-filtration]. Thus $g(F^pY)$ lies in the summands with $n\ge p$, which Step 1 identifies with $F^pI$. This proves the extension assertion without assuming enough injectives in $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Tag 05TR, lemma-injective-property-filtered-injective, proved componentwise using 05TP instead of its pushout proof

proof.text: Now assume enough injectives and fix any bounds $a\le b$ with $F^aX=X$, $F^{b+1}X=0$; such bounds exist for every finite filtration [def-sp-filtration], enlarging the interval if necessary. For each $a\le n\le b$ choose a monomorphism $e_n:X/F^{n+1}X\hookrightarrow E_n$ into an injective object, exactly as allowed by the enough-injectives hypothesis. Form the finite biproduct $E=\bigoplus_{n=a}^b E_n$ [def-sp-abelian] and give it the filtration $F^pE=\bigoplus_{n\ge p}E_n$, restricting indices to $[a,b]$. Define $v:X\to E$ by components $v_n=e_nq_n$. If $n<p$, then $q_n$ vanishes on $F^pX$, so $v$ preserves filtration. Direct projection onto the $p$th summand identifies $F^pE/F^{p+1}E$ with $E_p$ for $a\le p\le b$; outside the interval that quotient is zero. Zero is injective because all maps into it are the unique zero map [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Thus $E$ is filtered injective, and by construction $F^aE=E$ and $F^{b+1}E=0$.

The last coordinate $v_b=e_bq_b=e_b$ is monic since $F^{b+1}X=0$, so $v$ is monic. For $a<p\le b+1$, projection from $E$ to its summands with $n<p$ has kernel $F^pE$. Its composite with $v$ has kernel $F^pX$: the coordinate $n=p-1$ has exactly that kernel, since $e_{p-1}$ is monic, and all coordinates $n<p$ vanish on $F^pX$. Therefore $v^{-1}(F^pE)=F^pX$, equivalently $v(X)\cap F^pE=v(F^pX)$ as $v$ is monic. For $p\le a$, both filtrations are the whole object, so the same equality holds; for $p>b+1$, both steps are zero and monicity again gives it. These kernel and finite-projection computations use [def-sp-abelian] and [def-sp-filtration] only. Thus $v$ is strict and retains the prescribed bounds, proving the remaining assertions. If $a=b$, $v$ is just $e_a:X\hookrightarrow E_a$ in a single filtration degree. The zero object may be embedded into zero throughout.

lean.statement: theorem enough_strict_filtered_injectives : (∀ {X Y I : FilteredObject C} (hX : X.filtration.IsFinite) (hY : Y.filtration.IsFinite) (hI : I.filtration.IsFinite) (u : X ⟶ Y) [Mono u.hom], (∀ p : ℤ, imageSubobject ((X.filtration.step p).arrow ≫ u.hom) = imageSubobject u.hom ⊓ Y.filtration.step p) → (∀ p : ℤ, Injective (I.filtration.gradedPiece p)) → ∀ f : X ⟶ I, ∃ g : Y ⟶ I, u ≫ g = f) ∧ (EnoughInjectives C → ∀ X : FilteredObject C, X.filtration.IsFinite → ∃ (I : FilteredObject C) (v : X ⟶ I), I.filtration.IsFinite ∧ Mono v.hom ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, imageSubobject ((X.filtration.step p).arrow ≫ v.hom) = imageSubobject v.hom ⊓ I.filtration.step p) ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, Injective (I.filtration.gradedPiece p))) ∧ (EnoughInjectives C → ∀ (X : FilteredObject C) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b → X.filtration.step a = ⊤ → X.filtration.step (b + 1) = ⊥ → ∃ (I : FilteredObject C) (v : X ⟶ I), Mono v.hom ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, imageSubobject ((X.filtration.step p).arrow ≫ v.hom) = imageSubobject v.hom ⊓ I.filtration.step p) ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, Injective (I.filtration.gradedPiece p)) ∧ I.filtration.step a = ⊤ ∧ I.filtration.step (b + 1) = ⊥)
